second_probe.why_it_matters: The same account, twenty minutes later, returned the frame the fixture was built to describe: status 'allowed', rateLimitType 'five_hour', five_hour at 2 % — and the call refused anyway. The pre-ADR-364 gate reads room here and dispatches F6's create prompt. The first probe's 'rejected' status was luck, and it did not repeat.

third_probe.why_it_matters: Still refused, two hours after the second probe, on the same org_level_disabled setting — and the frames arrived in the other order: an allowed five_hour frame in front of the rejected seven_day_overage_included one. The reading took the first frame, so the receipt said `five_hour, allowed, resets 2026-09-16T19:20Z` beside `room: false`, and dropped the 100 % overage window that is the reason for the refusal. ADR-369 reads the frame that rejected.

adr_369_reading_names.resets_at_is: the schedule of the seven_day_overage_included usage window, not a date for the org_level_disabled setting that refused this probe

fourth_probe.why_it_matters: Still refused, on the same org_level_disabled setting, four hours after the third probe: F6 cannot be dispatched. Reading the gate that will decide the dispatch when capacity returns found the other half of ADR-369 unfixed (ADR-376). On an *answered* probe the reading was still the first frame, so the stray rejected seven_day_overage_included frame this organisation emits on every probe decided the verdict whenever the provider sent it first: the same answered probe at five_hour 8 % reads allowed and dispatches with the allowed frame in front, and rejected and defers with the rejected frame in front. That would have withheld F6 and F7 from a model that would have answered, for as long as overage stays disabled.

adr_376_defect.applies_to: an answered probe, not this refused one
adr_376_defect.fixed: the reading is the frame that bound the call: rejected on a refused probe, allowed on an answered one

fifth_probe.why_it_matters: Still refused, an hour after the fourth probe, on the same org_level_disabled setting: F6 cannot be dispatched, and the run's configured stop (2026-09-17T04:25:13Z) falls more than a day before this window's scheduled reset. This is also the first live reading taken with the ADR-369/ADR-376 gate in place on the frame order that broke the third probe: the provider put the allowed five_hour frame first and the rejected seven_day_overage_included frame second, and the gate named the rejecting frame anyway.
